title: Tx time module migration
summary: Create a physical tx-time crate, move timekeeper/VVAR/typed RTC and the opaque-key timer engine into it, and retain concrete deadline-domain ownership and routing in tx-reactor.

write_sets.notes: This proposed plan owns its plan documents only. Each implementation phase must claim its code write set in an isolated worktree before it starts; coordinate STATUS.md updates with the existing active plan owner.

external_refs: Linux clocksource, clockevent, timekeeping, and hrtimer separation

steps.title: Add tx-time and convert tx-services time to compatibility re-exports
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-13: tx-time has only tx-hal/tx-substrate dependencies; tx-services remains a compatibility facade. Added three tx-time API/role/error tests and forwarded workspace lints. Verification passed: cargo check -p tx-time -p tx-services; cargo test -p tx-time --lib (3); cargo test -p tx-services --lib time (7); diff check.

steps.title: Move timekeeper, VVAR contents/publication, and typed RTC adapters
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-13: tx_time::keeper is the sole timekeeper and VVAR payload owner; tx-services wall_clock is a compatibility re-export. VVAR page/frame/mapping remain in tx-subsystems, which rejects stale generations. Hooks execute after the keeper writer lock drops; Required writeback failures and invalid calibration are rejected. Verification passed: cargo check -p tx-time -p tx-services -p tx-subsystems; cargo test -p tx-time --lib (12); service wall_clock test (1); subsystem vdso tests (2); diff check. The recorded tx-fs selector exited 0 but matched no test in this checkout.

steps.title: Implement TimerEngine behind a private indexed min-heap queue
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: indexed min-heap engine stores opaque key/deadline state only. Added cancellation, rearm, stale expiry, swap-remove index repair, key exhaustion, lock-external growth/output reservation, and panic-safe growth restoration. Verification passed: 15 focused timer tests; 25 full tx-time tests; cargo check -p tx-time; diff check.

steps.title: Add reactor-owned timer domain, route table, and post-lock routing
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: ReactorTimerDomain owns the new engine, private routes, domain-backed registrar, single-driver claim, deadline-change state, stale/cancelled suppression, and post-drain delivery. Legacy TimerWheel remains only as compatibility/script backend. Verification passed: tx-time 25, tx-services 4, reactor domain 5, reactor_smoke timer 7, timer_idle 4, v3_timer_surface 18, v3_pr7b_timer_routing 9, cargo checks, and diff check.

steps.title: Route HAL deadline programming through reactor timer-domain driver
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: thread_future no longer programs HalDeadlineTimer; POSIX/ITIMER scans retain semantic registrar rearm but discard their observation rather than registering it again. Reactor driver owns current-hart arm/cancel from domain next deadline. Verified thread_future 26, hart_loop 7, reactor_smoke timer 7, concurrent restore and HartId(3) arm witnesses, cargo checks, and diff check.

steps.title: Migrate timerfd, POSIX/ITIMER, futex, epoll, scripts, and RTC consumers
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: semantic consumers register only through the public DeadlineDomain facade. Timerfd uses WaitSource, POSIX/ITIMER use SignalTarget, futex/epoll/scripts use task/delegate deadlines, and RTC emulation uses DeviceCallback. Timerfd 10, POSIX 4, fd 20, ioctl 19, all tx-shims 592, and devfs 22 tests passed.

steps.title: Delete old timer registry and ratchet import boundary lints
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: removed substrate TimerWheel, registrar/router types, reactor legacy dual-fire path, driver compatibility exports, and script adapter residue. TimerEngine plus ReactorTimerDomain is the only queue/routing topology. Both time invariants passed with zero findings, including xtask source scanning.

steps.title: Run host/QEMU gates and close the migration record
steps.notes: Completed 2026-07-14: tx-time 27, reactor timer surfaces 3+2, tx-shims 592, devfs 22, and scoped checks passed. RV64 full-build and QEMU smoke passed with boot and SMP owner-wake sentinels. Deferred network, board RTC, CPU/TAI, and full VDSO work remain out of scope.

verification.notes: Passed 2026-07-14 after closing the migration record.
Passed 2026-07-14; seven pre-existing stale-vocabulary warnings remain non-fatal.

risks: Queue callbacks or mailbox posts under an engine lock can reintroduce lock inversion and stale owner routing.
A missing driver claim or earlier-deadline reprogram path can double-fire or oversleep under SMP.
Moving only timerfd delivery without preserving object-owned periodic/rebase state can regress Linux semantics.
Conflating RTC device alarms with task timeouts can break poll and epoll readiness.
The dirty workspace can make broad host or QEMU failures unrelated to this migration.
